key_insight: Closed-loop validation-repair dramatically improved clinical LLM schema compliance, pushing interoperability-ready outputs to about 99% across three models.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a practical safeguard for EHR-linked AI systems that need outputs conforming to healthcare standards like ICD-10, CPT, and HL7 FHIR.
method: Locally deployed Qwen2.5 7B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Gemma2 9B
Tested 320 clinical scenarios across 10 specialties (960 model-scenario pairs)
Compared baseline outputs with a validation-repair loop for schema compliance
evidence_signal: Baseline compliance was 85.9% to 91.6%, while validation-repair increased overall compliance to 99.0% (98.4% to 99.4%) with McNemar p<0.001.
watch_item: The findings focus on schema correctness, so real-world deployment still needs careful checking for clinical accuracy, workflow fit, and standard-specific edge cases.
paper_title: Closed-Loop Validation-Repair for Healthcare Interoperability: A Multi-Model Study of Schema Compliance in Clinical LLMs
